rationale: Post-migration SEO invisibility is a real and high-stakes pain — losing branded search traffic after a domain move directly costs revenue — and indie developers and bootstrapped founders demonstrably pay for SEO tools at $99–449/mo (Ahrefs, Semrush). Buildability is strong: a domain-migration SEO audit is something Claude can generate as a structured checklist report from a URL + GSC data, packaged as a one-time or subscription deliverable, with delivery fully automated. Operational autonomy meets the build gate floor (7): intake via form, report generated by Claude, delivered by email, billing via Stripe. The two weaknesses are pain frequency (migration is episodic, not daily — score 4) and responsiveness being untested. Validate first with a targeted outreach to post-migration founders before committing to build.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a 'Domain Migration SEO Audit Report' — a buyer submits their old domain, new domain, and a GSC data export via a form, and within 24 hours Claude produces a structured diagnosis report covering redirect coverage, canonical tags, internal link updates, GSC property settings, and a ranked action list. The factory builds this as: Claude prompt (audit logic) + a Tally/Typeform intake form + automated email delivery + a Stripe one-time payment link ($49–99 per audit); no coding by Youval. To sell: reach founders who recently posted about domain migrations on IndieHackers, r/webdev, or r/SEO, or who appear in GSC community threads — all outreach approved before sending; also post a free 'migration checklist' on IndieHackers as a lead magnet linking to the paid audit. Once live, every step (payment, intake, report generation, delivery) runs via Claude + code; Youval's only recurring touch is approving outreach batches. The key risk is that pain frequency is low (most buyers only migrate once), so this works best as a one-time purchase funnel rather than a subscription — test whether a 'post-migration monitoring' add-on ($15/mo) can extend LTV.
notes: All build gates met at or above minimums (operational_autonomy 7, buildability_with_ai 8, buyer_clarity 6, willingness_to_pay 6). Low pain_frequency (episodic migration event) is the main LTV risk — validate demand depth before investing in a subscription model. Total 5.9 qualifies for validate; a successful probe pushing responsiveness to 6+ would support promotion to build.
